questions.q: Which rule is mandatory for an interrupt handler?

questions.q: Why is blocking code in the control loop a disaster?
options: It heats the CPU and lowers the voltage
It breaks the interrupt vector table
questions.explain: Loops are missed: stale gyro data, D-term jumps, a possible watchdog reboot.

questions.q: What happens to the sensor task's jitter if a higher-priority task busy-waits for 5 ms?
questions.explain: A preemptive scheduler gives the core to the higher-priority task.

questions.q: Why must you not call printf in an interrupt handler?
options: It is slow and blocking, and delays the other interrupts
It does not compile on an STM32
Interrupts have no access to memory
questions.explain: An ISR must be short: slow and blocking calls break the timing of the whole system.
